newsitem.title: USA: Defeated N.Y. Republican fades from view.
newsitem.headline: Defeated N.Y. Republican fades from view.

text.p: New York Representative Dan Frisa, defeated last month by a gun control activist with no experience in politics, has yet to make the traditional concession speech or phone call, according to the winner.
In fact, three weeks after the Nov. 5 election, the one-term Republican House member from suburban Long Island has scarcely been heard from, his supporters say.

Frisa was defeated by Democrat Carolyn McCarthy, who became a gun control lobbyist after her husband was killed and her son wounded in 1993 by a gunman on a local commuter train. She chose to run after Frisa, with National Rifle Association support, voted for repeal of the assault weapons ban.

Frisa failed to show up at his campaign headquarters on election night for a concession speech and has yet to appear, said supporter Henry Poisnet of the American Legion Post in Westbury, New York, which donated its meeting hall and volunteers for the event.
"We think it's awful the way he handled it. He just disappointed us by not even coming to say thanks," Poisnet said.
His campaign left behind a Congressional seal that legion members vow to keep until Frisa apologises, Poisnet said.
Frisa faded from the public eye several days before the election, relying on a mail campaign, turning down personal appearances and not returning calls from members of the media.
On election night, he emerged briefly from his home to accuse McCarthy of campaign exaggerations and to call the assault weapons ban "a lie."
Defying tradition, Frisa has yet to make the usual congratulatory call to the victor, McCarthy said this week.
"I never heard from him," she said. "I don't think he ever took me seriously. It came as a shock to him," she said of her victory. "It came as a shock to me."
Calls to Frisa's office were not returned.
